$comment: Canonical theme-conformance contract — the single source of truth for both
the static guard (scripts/lint-css.mjs, rules 5, 6 and 7) and the runtime
guard (scripts/check-theme.ts), so the two can never disagree.
WHICH THEMES EXIST IS NOT DECIDED HERE. registry.json's `themes` array is
the source of truth; this file adds the per-theme CONTRACT (which colours
are forbidden, which templates are exempt). lint-css.mjs fails if the two
lists disagree, so a theme cannot be added to one and forgotten in the
other.
Brand authority: https://brand.devfellowship.com (mirror at /llms.txt) for
DFL, /itera/llms.txt and /revera/llms.txt for the two sub-brands, chapter
'03 · Cor' of each. A theme file is the CSS implementation of one of those
guides; a template is 'on theme' when it reads the tokens instead of
restating their values.
WHY THE FORBIDDEN LISTS EXIST. Every template reads its tokens as
var(--s-token, <literal>), and every literal is the DevFellowship value.
That fallback is load-bearing — it keeps a template renderable standalone —
but it means a theme that fails to define a token does not fail loudly: the
template silently paints the DFL colour instead. That is exactly how a deck
set to the 'default' theme rendered in DevFellowship dark until 2026-08-12
(themes/default.css defined ZERO --s-* tokens). Asserting 'the surface is
the theme's surface' catches it on .tpl-root; asserting 'no element
computes to another brand's colour' catches it everywhere else.
literalExceptions are the ONLY places a raw colour may appear in template
CSS outside a var() fallback. Keep the list tiny; every entry needs a
rationale. Same discipline as fluidTemplates in canvas.config.json.
$tokenRoleComment: The tokens whose resolved value the runtime guard reads back from the
browser to know what THIS theme's surface / ink / accent actually are. It
never hardcodes a colour per theme: it asks the injected CSS. So a theme
cannot pass by agreeing with a stale number in this file.
$fontComment: The four families of brand chapter 06. Every element that renders text must
resolve to one of these as its first computed font-family — which happens
for free when the declaration is var(--s-font-display|body|mono|editorial).
Type is NOT themed: all four themes declare the same four families, because
a sub-brand changes colour and never type.
$forbiddenComment: Per theme: colours that must never appear in a render of that theme, with
the rule from the brand guide that says so.
`accents` are matched AT ANY ALPHA. An accent tint is a palette entry, and
the theme owns a token for it (--s-brand-subtle / --s-brand-border /
--s-brand-ring), so a translucent Itera-green wash on a Revera slide is the
same defect as an opaque one.
`surfaces` are matched ONLY WHEN OPAQUE. This is deliberate, and it is the
same distinction lint-css.mjs rule 5 already draws: a translucent colour is
a compositing value (a scrim over a photograph, a hairline, the dotted page
texture), not a palette entry. `full-bleed` and `chapter-image` legitimately
paint rgba(10, 9, 8, 0.1 … 0.95) over a photograph in EVERY theme, light
one included — a photograph is not a themed surface, and the ink over it
comes from --s-ink-on-media for exactly that reason. An OPAQUE DFL surface
on the light theme is the reported bug and nothing else.

accents.#E07A4A: DFL amber. The light theme's accent is --p-azure-600; amber here means a template fell through to its var() fallback.

surfaces.#0a0908: DFL sand-950 page surface. THIS is the reported bug: with themes/default.css defining no tokens, every template's .tpl-root fell back to this literal and a 'Default' deck rendered DevFellowship dark. On unmodified origin/main this assertion fails on 45 of 46 templates.
surfaces.#f6f1e7: DFL sand-50 — the DARK theme's primary ink. Near-white text on a near-white page: invisible, and the surest sign the ink token did not resolve.

accents.#3FD17F: Itera evergreen. Sub-brand accents do not appear on a DFL house slide (DFL guide ch. 17 family rules).

accents.#E07A4A: DFL amber. Itera guide 3.2 lists it under 'Proibidos em surface Itera' — 'só em co-branding by DFL'. No template emits a co-branding mark, so on a slide it can only be a fallback leak.
accents.#3D8FE0: Revera trust-blue. Itera guide 3.2: 'exclusivo Revera · não vaza pra Itera'.
accents.#00FF88: Saturated neon. Itera guide 3.2: 'nunca · neon não é Itera'.

$note: #5EC27E is listed in the Itera guide under 'Proibidos' with the
qualifier 'só status semântico', so it is NOT forbidden here: it is the
value of --s-success-* in every dark theme, and a green tick in
`checklist` is a status, not the Itera accent. Forbidding it would fail
a render that follows the guide.

accents.#3FD17F: Itera evergreen. Revera guide 3.2: 'exclusivo Itera · não vaza'.
accents.#0066FF: Electric blue. Revera guide 3.2: 'nunca · SaaS slop'.
accents.#00D4FF: Saturated neon. Revera guide 3.2: 'nunca · neon não é Revera'.

$note: DFL amber #E07A4A is deliberately NOT forbidden on Revera. Guide 3.4
keeps it as the ancestral 'by DFL' filiation mark, once per surface —
themes/revera.css defines it as --s-filiation-solid. It is still never
a CTA and never a KPI, which is a rule about which token a template
reads, not about which colour lands on the page.

blank.rationale: The 'screen + webcam only' recording backdrop. It must be true black, not the sand-950 page surface, because the recorder composites captured video over it and any warm tint would show at the seams. Same template, same reason, as its fluidTemplates entry in canvas.config.json.

$surfaceExceptionComment: A template whose .tpl-root is deliberately NOT the theme page surface.
`value` is either one computed colour (the same in every theme) or an
object keyed by theme id when the exception is theme-specific.

blank.rationale: See literalExceptions.blank — true-black recording backdrop, in every theme including the light one. The backdrop exists to be composited under captured video, so it does not follow the deck's palette.
